MUTATIONS: a login is kept only at the generation it started at; kept at any, a login in flight across a sign-out would store its key again and the sign-out would not hold (SPEC-363 A2)
a send needs the generation the sender holds to be current; without it, a Worker that read its key before a removal would still send it (SPEC-363 A3)
a send needs a sealed record stored at that generation; without it, a send would go out with no stored key behind it (SPEC-363 A3)
only the sync server's refusal classifies as refused; with every decoded kind refused, a network or server-message failure would drop the owner's key (SPEC-363 A4)
a refusal drops the key only when it refused the current generation; without the clause, a late refusal of an older key would drop the new login's key (SPEC-363 A5)
a removal names the next generation; returning the one it was given, a login in flight across the removal would be kept (SPEC-363 A6)
the generation never wraps at its maximum; wrapping, it would fall to zero and an old login's generation would read as current again (SPEC-363 A6)
the sealing key is the HMAC of the label then the seal id; unlabelled, the key would be the bare HMAC of the id under a secret another use could share (SPEC-363 A9)
a seal secret under 32 bytes refuses start; accepted, a short secret would seal every web client's key under a guessable key (SPEC-363 A10)
the release answers an owner session alone; without the extractor, a link session or no session at all would receive the sealing key (SPEC-363 A11)
a seal id parses only from 16 decoded bytes; without the test, an id of another length would be read and the parse would not hold its shape (SPEC-363 A18)
the release admits 30 in a minute and refuses the 31st; at 3000, a stolen session could draw keys for many seal ids before any bound held (SPEC-363 A13)
the released key is answered no-store; as private, a browser cache would keep the sealing key on disk (SPEC-363 A14)
the release refuses a cross-site or non-JSON request; without the guard, another site could make the owner's browser ask for the key (SPEC-363 A14)
with no seal secret the route answers 404 sync_seal_off; otherwise it would release keys made from a secret nobody configured (SPEC-363 A15)
an absent seal secret turns the release off and the API still starts; refused, a host with no seal secret would not start the API at all (SPEC-363 A17)
the API role composes the seal secret it reads; dropped, a host that holds the secret would still answer the release off, and no web client could keep its sync key sealed (SPEC-363 B14)
